newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends sharply lower on dlr short-cover.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends sharply lower on dlr short-cover.

text.p: The won closed Tuesday's hectic trading sharply lower on late dollar short-covering after an expected intervention by the central bank did not materialise, dealers said.
The won closed at a day low of 822.00 after opening at 819.60. It hit a high of 819.30.
Dealers said some banks cautiously bought the U.S. currency to push it up over 820.00, the level where many had believed the central bank would step in.
The lack of action was "against our expectation. Shorts seem to have been damaged today," a local bank dealer said.
He said a government procurement deal worth $56 million also boosted the early dollar strength.
"The market has been short due to accumulated importer deals in the past days," said another local bank dealer.
Dealers expected the won to open weak on Wednesday on the tail of today's dollar buying sentiment, but said the central bank would decide the market direction.
They said the won could fall to the 825.00 level if there is no intervention. But its rise was seen limited to 820.00.
Wednesday's mid-rate is expected to be pegged at 820.00 or 820.10 against 819.30 today. -- Y.J. YEOM 727 5647
